title.narrative: Integrated Health and Nutrition Emergency Response in Abergele and Gazgibla woredas of the Waghimira zone in Amhara region

description.narrative: ltpgtOver the past 5 years, the Waghimira zone of the Amhara region have experienced deteriorating humanitarian conditions due to conflict, drought, flooding, disease outbreaks, and pest infestations. There are 136,749 (Female 94,357) people affected by the natural disaster in Abergele ltspangtand Gazgibla lt/spangtltspangtworedas lt/spangtltspangt(MIRA, 2024). Women, children, and PWDs are disproportionately affected both the natural disasters and conflict. A recent assessment revealt/spangtltspangtled that 56% of PLW are moderately malnourished, while children under five are increasingly at risk due to the lack of nutritional supplements and adequate food. Ongoing conflict and disrupted supply chains continue to exacerbate food insecurity, heightening vulnerability among these high-risk groups (PAD, 2025).lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtHealth and nutrition services in these woredas are severely under-resourced. Over 60% of health facilities are either non-functional or only partially operational due to damage, shortages of medical supplies, or the absence of trained personnel (MIRA, 2024 PAD, 2025). Maternal health services and child nutrition programs are especially weak. The shortage of IYCF materials has further worsened the conditions of malnourished mothers and children. The health infrastructure is in urgent need of rehabilitation, and these constraints are limiting access to critical, life-saving services for women, children, and the elderly, leaving them vulnerable to preventable health risks.ltbrgtRecent nutrition assessments highlight critical levels of GAM: 39% in Abergele, and 47% in Gaz Gibla. MAM rates are reported at 31.5% and 40.14% for Abergele and Gaz Gibla Woredas respectively (PAD, 2025). These figures exceed emergency thresholds and signal a nutrition crisis that demands an urgent response. PAD, in collaboration with local authorities, will implement integrated health and nutrition interventions to reduce malnutrition, morbidity, and mortality among the most vulnerable, children under 5, PLW, and PWDs aligned with the 2024 HRP.ltbrgtThe proposed project will address urgent humanitarian needs in Abergele and Gaz Gibla woredas. These areas have been severely impacted by conflict and recurrent drought, leading to a significant decline in health and nutritional well-being. Multiple assessments conducted by both internal teams and external actors have identified critical service delivery gaps, underscoring the need for immediate and coordinated humanitarian action.ltbrgtThe project will deliver essential, life-saving health and nutrition interventions, prioritizing women, children, and PWDs. A total of 35,319 conflict- and drought-affected individuals, including 21,219 women, will directly benefit. Of these, 16893 people (Female 8706) will access health services, while 18,426 individuals (Female 12,513) will receive targeted nutrition support. Additionally, 3389 PWDs will receive inclusive support tailored to their needs.ltbrgtHealth interventions will include primary healthcare services, disease prevention, maternal and child health care, and health education. Nutrition support will focus on the prevention and treatment of acute malnutrition among children under five and PLW. Both components will include community outreach, training for health workers, and collaboration with local health authorities to strengthen service delivery systems.ltbrgtThe project will engage closely with local government structures, community leaders, and sector offices to ensure strong coordination, promote community ownership, and achieve sustainability. Risk management strategies such as ongoing security assessments, clear communication protocols, and emergency preparedness will safeguard staff and beneficiaries. With a total budget of USD 300,000.00, this 9-month project represents a critical investment in the health and resilience of highly vulnerable communities. The budget will support health and nutrition service delivery, capacity building, community engagement, and robust monitoring and evaluation. ltbrgtlt/pgt
